title: Avoid Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Using a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage transition is a common mistake that causes frequent clogs and poor flow velocity. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or vent connections. When used horizontally, the sharp turn disrupts waste momentum and permits solids to settle near the branch junction. For horizontal drain branch transitions, plumbing codes require long-sweep combination wye fittings or a standard wye with an eighth bend. This design maintains smooth directional flow, reduces hydraulic jump, and keeps solids moving through the drainage system efficiently. Always verify fitting direction and local code requirements during rough-in visual inspections.
